target_customer: Canadian men seeking prescription treatment for erectile dysfunction, hair loss, weight management and related conditions, paying out of pocket
problem: Men in Canada face stigma and slow access when seeking care for sensitive conditions; Phoenix offers provider-reviewed virtual care with prescriptions filled by partner pharmacies.
business_model: Direct-to-consumer telehealth clinic with consultation and prescription revenue through partner pharmacies

founders.name: Kevin Bache
founders.background_notes: YC page: over a decade in software development, design, digital health and pharmaceutical advertising.

founders.name: Gavin Thompson
founders.background_notes: YC page: senior software developer who built products for Walmart and Disney.

competitors.name: Maple
competitors.what: Toronto virtual care provider offering on-demand consultations
competitors.traction_then: Toronto HQ expected to triple in size over two years per the company's 2019 announcement

technical_complexity.rationale: Telehealth intake, prescribing workflow and pharmacy integration; regulatory and clinical operations were harder than the software.

defensibility.rationale: Provincial licensing of physicians gives some friction, but similar clinics could copy the model and customers have few switching costs.

incumbents: US men's telehealth brands such as Hims and Roman
takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Phoenix raised a 50 million Canadian dollar Series A in 2025 and launched a sister women's brand, Raven.

market_need_then: Pandemic-era adoption of telehealth in Canada and the stigma around ED and hair loss care; Maple's 2022 interview anticipated post-peak telehealth demand declines. No dated Canadian men's telehealth demand figure was opened.

branding.domain_note: Owns phoenix.ca, a short Canadian domain.

identity.logo: A phoenix avatar icon appears in app mockups on the site
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, reassuring and cheeky; tagline Men's health made simple; ad campaigns use innuendo around the idea of rising again

branding.brand_signature: The Rise Again Super Bowl ad campaign (Multiple Positions, February 2024)
branding.community_and_virality: First national campaign aired during the Canadian Super Bowl telecast in February 2024 and a second ad in February 2025, covered by Adweek, Campaign Canada, Strategy and LBB.

brand_strength.rationale: Two Super Bowl ads with trade press coverage and a name that matches the pitch of renewal; only a few years of brand history and the origin of the name is not stated.

outcome_analysis: Phoenix grew from a Winter 2021 YC start to about 70 staff and a 50 million Canadian dollar Series A in March 2025 led by Valspring, with a launched sister brand and a generic semaglutide offering announced in 2026. The growth rests on cash-pay telehealth demand and unusually visible advertising. Earlier rounds and valuation are not public in the sources found.
notes: The round is stated in Canadian dollars (50 million) so amount_usd is null; BetaKit says it was mostly equity with an undisclosed split and valuation. Finsmes labels it Series C, other outlets Series A, the company release says Series A. BetaKit says total funding is 55 million while aggregators list 34.8 to 38.7 million (conflict). The 2021 seed is only an aggregator entry (125,000 dollars, Goodwater and YC), which is the standard YC deal, so it is not recorded as a round. Education of founders not stated on sources opened. The Maple competitor source is a 2019 funding announcement; Roman and Hims in Canada were not confirmed.
